svg.text: Who may reach whose data, and why
Four sources of access, one shape. Three are derived live from records the bank already keeps, so they cannot drift. Only delegation is stored, because only delegation is a human decision.
PRINCIPALS sec.app_user
One row per login. Two kinds, kept apart
by a check constraint:
STAFF user_type = relationship_manager
risk, administrator ...
subject_client_id IS NULL. Reach comes
from the books granted to them.
CUSTOMER user_type = client
subject_client_id IS NOT NULL.
The principal IS that one client.
There is no book to widen.
Never both, never neither.
Without the constraint, giving a staff user a
subject_client_id adds a client silently.
THE GRANT SET sec.v_access_grant
ownership derived
The principal IS this client, and owns these
accounts. From core.bridge_disposition, is_owner.
view + operate, on the client AND their accounts
disposition derived
Authorised to operate an account they do NOT own.
From the source dispositions of type DISPONENT.
view + operate, ON THAT ACCOUNT ONLY
not the owner's client record, not their other accounts
portfolio derived
Staff, through a book granted to them.
From sec.portfolio_client + sec.user_portfolio.
view ONLY — accountability is not payment authority
delegation STORED sec.access_delegation
A human decision: power of attorney, holiday cover,
a court order. The only source with no other record.
Demands a grantor, a reason and usually an expiry
RESOLUTION the one place auth meets access
sec.v_my_clients / sec.v_my_accounts
Filters the grant set to session_user — which no
statement can change — and to grants inside their
validity window.
AND sec.has_verified_session()
An AND over the WHOLE resolution, not a filter inside
one branch — so a branch added later cannot quietly
skip the second factor.
ENFORCEMENT 7 row level security policies
dim_client · dim_account · bridge_disposition · dim_card
fact_loan · fact_transaction · fact_account_month_end_balance
Each asks the resolution views one question:
"which clients / accounts may the caller see?"
No policy knows that customer logins exist.
Adding the client grain cost one column and one UNION.
It changed no policy and no consumer view — which is
the test that the filter really does live in one place.
The same account, reached two ways — account 3112 (CZ84 8888 0000 0000 0000 3112)
client_3763 · ownership · view + operate
She owns it. She also sees her own client record (BRK-TQ8D-RCB3).
client_3764 · disposition · view + operate
He may use it. He CANNOT see her client record, or anything else of hers.
rm_north · portfolio · view
Both customers are in her book. She sees both; neither sees the other.
rm_south · delegation · view · expires in 14 days
"Covering the northern book while rm_north is on leave" — granted by head_of_retail.
sec.v_who_can_reach_client answers the privacy question from the model, not from anyone's memory:
for any client — every principal who can reach them, which permission, from which source, granted by whom, and until when.
Not shown, and absent on purpose: a record of who actually DID read a row. This model controls who CAN. The read audit is the largest missing control and is named as such in the build review.
The pipeline owner (berka_owner) owns these tables and is exempt from their policies, which is what makes the build possible. It is a deployment identity, never an application login.
"Sees everything" (admin_demo, cro_global) is a portfolio containing every client — granted through data, visible in the view above. It is not a privilege, and rolbypassrls is false.
